pr.title: coverage: Build an "expansion tree" and use it to unexpand raw spans
pr.description:
Historically and currently, coverage instrumentation assumes that all of a function's spans are in the same file and have the same syntax context. The spans extracted directly from MIR don't satisfy that assumption, so there is an “unexpansion” step that walks up each span's expansion-call-site tree to find a suitable span in the same context as the function's body span.

(That unexpansion step is what allows us to have somewhat reasonable coverage instrumentation for macros like `println!`, and for syntax like `for` and `?` that undergo desugaring expansion.)

The current unexpansion code mostly works fine in that “flat” single-file single-context world. But it's not suitable for incremental work towards proper expansion-aware coverage instrumentation, which would allow a function's coverage spans to encompass multiple expansion contexts and multiple files.

This PR therefore replaces the current unexpansion code with a more sophisticated system that uses the raw MIR spans to reconstruct an “expansion tree”, and then uses that tree to help perform most of the unexpansion work.

Building the tree is “overkill” for current unexpansion needs (though it does give some minor edge-case improvements), but my hope is that having the explicit tree available will be a big help when taking the next steps towards proper expansion-region support.
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.originalLogic: The pre-PR coverage refinement took each `RawSpanFromMir` independently and called `unexpand_into_body_span_with_expn_kind(raw_span, body_span)`, which walked `parent_callsite()` until the span was contained in `body_span` and had the same syntax context. It then sorted by dominator order, deduplicated repeated await/bang-macro spans by span equality, and shrank visible bang-macro spans through `!`. The PR replaces this flat per-span pipeline with an `ExpnTree` keyed by `ExpnId`: each raw `SpanWithBcb` is attached to its span's `ctxt().outer_expn()` node, and the tree is linked upward by the call site's `outer_expn()`. Refinement then emits the body node's own spans plus at most one distilled covspan per child expansion.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The source-explicit wrong rewrite is to build the expansion tree's parent links from `ExpnData::parent` instead of from `ExpnData::call_site`. The patch instead stores the non-dummy `call_site`, filters dummy spans, and sets `call_site_expn_id` from `call_site.ctxt().outer_expn()`. With parent-based lineage, child expansions whose parent differs from their call-site context (for example under `#[rustfmt::skip]`) are not reachable from the body expansion node, so `single_covspan_for_child_expn` is never called for them and macros such as `println!(...)` are not instrumented. This is distinct from the older flat per-span unexpansion, which is the replaced baseline and still walked `parent_callsite`; the parent-based tree linkage is the named incorrect transformation guarded by the new regression test.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions compiled with coverage instrumentation whose MIR contains spans from expansion contexts: bang macros (`println!`, `assert!`, `trace!`), desugaring (`await`, `for`, `?`), macro invocations inside closures, multi-line macro invocations with the call site and arguments on separate lines, functions annotated `#[rustfmt::skip]`, and expansions with dummy or non-dummy call sites. Raw spans may be in a different syntax context or file from the function body span.
analysis.trigger: A raw MIR span has `ctxt().outer_expn()` different from `body_span.ctxt().outer_expn()`, especially when a child expansion's call-site span belongs to the body expansion's context. The failure specifically appears when tree parentage is derived from `ExpnData::parent` rather than from the call-site span's outer expansion.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation has extracted raw MIR spans with associated BCBs.
The function body span is available as the root context.
Each expansion node derives `call_site` from `ExpnData::call_site`, discards dummy call sites, and derives `call_site_expn_id` via `call_site.ctxt().outer_expn()`.
Child expansions are registered under the expansion containing their call site.
The function may carry `#[rustfmt::skip]` or other metadata that can make `ExpnData::parent` differ from the call-site lineage.
pitfalls: Using `ExpnData::parent` for expansion-tree edges can silently drop macro instrumentation under `#[rustfmt::skip]`.
Treating a dummy `call_site` as a real parent can create bogus or unreachable nodes; the patch filters with `!sp.is_dummy()`.
Deduplicating await/bang-macro expansions by span alone loses extra child-expansion mappings; the new code selects one BCB per child expansion in dominator order.

BCB selection is kind-dependent: bang macros and `await` use `min_by` with `cmp_in_dominator_order`, while other expansions use `max_by` (most dominated). Reversing this changes which region receives the mapping.
Only bang-macro call-site spans should be truncated with `span_through_char(span, '!')`; applying that to other expansion kinds loses source text.
Use `contains`, `eq_ctxt`, and `source_equal` checks: discard spans outside the body and spans that fill the entire body.
Do not confuse missing macro instrumentation with borrowing restrictions or post-copy overwrites; this is about expansion-tree lineage.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a coverage snapshot test under `tests/coverage` with `//@ edition: 2024` and `#[rustfmt::skip] fn main()` containing a multi-line `println!` whose call site and string argument are on separate lines, plus a gap before the first statement. The expected `.coverage`/`.cov-map` should show distinct mappings for the function body, macro invocation/call site, and argument (the new `rustfmt-skip.cov-map` has four mappings) instead of only function-body coverage. The test comment explicitly says it detects building the tree from `ExpnData::parent` instead of `ExpnData::call_site`; a parent-linked variant should lose instrumentation of the `println!` expansions. Also update closure and macro-in-closure cov-map expectations when a child expansion gains its own call-site mapping.
analysis.summary: This is a coverage refactor/optimization, not a confirmed reproduced bug fix: it replaces flat per-span unexpansion with an expansion tree and per-child-expansion span distillation. The source-backed invariant is that tree edges must follow the non-dummy `ExpnData::call_site` context, never `ExpnData::parent`; otherwise macros such as `println!` can disappear from coverage. The added `rustfmt-skip` regression test and cov-map changes encode the expected extra macro call-site mappings. No compiler was built or executed.
